messages.content: Estou planejando um acampamento e preciso saber a previsão do tempo. Você pode me buscar os dados meteorológicos do acampamento localizado para os próximos 10 dias, incluindo previsões diárias de temperatura e precipitação? Além disso, prefiro a temperatura máxima de 2 minutos em Fahrenheit e a soma da precipitação em polegadas.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning: The user wants weather forecast for a camping location for next 10 days, including daily temperature and precipitation. They prefer maximum temperature at 2-minute resolution in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. We need to use the Open-Meteo API. The user didn't specify coordinates. We need to ask for location. Also we need to convert units: Open-Meteo returns Celsius and mm. We can request units=imperial to get Fahrenheit and inches? Let's check Open-Meteo API: It supports parameter "temperature_unit" maybe? Actually Open-Meteo supports "temperature_unit=fahrenheit" and "precipitation_unit=inch". But the function signature only includes latitude, longitude, elevation. No unit parameters. So we cannot pass units. But we can request default units (Celsius, mm). Then we can convert ourselves. But the function signature doesn't allow specifying units. So we can't request Fahrenheit directly. We could still call the API with default units and then convert. But the user specifically wants Fahrenheit and inches. We can fetch data and then convert. But we need to know the location. So we should ask for coordinates. Also we need to ask for the location name. So we will ask for latitude and longitude. Also we might ask for elevation if needed. But we can just ask for location name and let them provide coordinates. We'll ask for latitude and longitude. Then we can call the API. The function signature requires "params" with latitude, longitude, elevation optional. We'll call with those. Then we can process the JSON. We'll need to convert temperatures from Celsius to Fahrenheit: F = C * 9/5 + 32. Precipitation from mm to inches: inches = mm / 25.4. Then we can compute daily max temperature and sum precipitation. But the user wants maximum temperature at 2-minute resolution. That seems unrealistic: 2-minute resolution would require high-frequency data. Open-Meteo provides hourly data. There's no 2-minute resolution. So we can explain that we can provide hourly data and compute daily max. Or we can approximate. We'll ask for clarification. But we can proceed with hourly data. We'll ask for location coordinates.
